angle: Silver rounds give stackers the lowest premiums of any coin-shaped product — 5-10% over spot versus 20-25% for American Silver Eagles — making them the most efficient way to accumulate physical silver during the current multi-year supply deficit.

stats.claim: Silver rounds carry premiums of only 5–10% over spot price, compared to 20–25% over spot for American Silver Eagles and 15–20% for Canadian Silver Maple Leafs, making them the lowest-premium coin-shaped silver product available.
J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts silver prices will average $81 per ounce in 2026 — more than double the 2025 average of $40.10 per ounce — driven by industrial demand and supply deficits.
The silver market recorded its fifth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2025, with a shortfall of 95 million ounces, and cumulative deficits of nearly 820 million ounces from 2021 through 2025.

Global silver demand reached a record high of 1.20 billion ounces in the 2025 forecast, with industrial fabrication on track to surpass 700 million ounces for the first time ever, driven by solar and electronics demand.
stats.value: 1.20 billion oz total demand; 700M+ oz industrial

stats.claim: Silver bar and coin demand fell 4% in 2025 to 182 million ounces — a seven-year low — as higher prices pulled retail buyers to the sidelines even as ETF inflows surged.

On a $5,000 purchase, choosing 100 oz silver bars over American Silver Eagles can result in 8–12 additional ounces of silver for the same outlay; silver rounds at 5–10% premium represent the middle ground between bars and sovereign coins.
